title: Exact augmented resolution columns give a quasi-isomorphism to the total
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $K$ be a $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complex in $\mathcal A$, and let $I$ be a bicomplex [def-sp-double-complex-total] with complex degree $s\in\mathbf Z$ and resolution degree $r\in\mathbf N$. Let $a:K[0]\to I$ be a bicomplex map, where $K[0]$ means $K$ concentrated in resolution degree zero. Suppose $I^{s,\bullet}=0$ for $s<b$ for some $b\in\mathbf Z$, and each $a^s$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Extend the resolution degree by zero using [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], then exchange indices to obtain $J$. If a supplied chain map $\epsilon:K\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)$ has degree-$n$ component $a^{n,0}$ followed by the extension identification and the $(0,n)$ diagonal inclusion, then $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism. No injectivity hypothesis on the terms is made.

source.place: Lemma 12.25.4 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), together with Tag 015J, proof remark (3)

proof.text: Choose b below which I vanishes. Since each a^s is a quasi-isomorphism from K^s in degree zero, K^s is also zero below b. Extend resolution degree by zero and augment each resolution column with K^s in degree -1. Each augmented column is acyclic by the column quasi-isomorphism hypothesis. The augmentation commutes with the complex-degree differential because a is a bicomplex map.

Exchange the indices and totalize the augmented bicomplex. In degree n its object is Tot(I)^n plus K^{n+1}. The vertical differential on the K summand is exactly aug by the specified component equation, while the complex-degree differential on this summand has sign -1. These identities give an isomorphism from the augmented total to the actual mapping cone of aug. All its diagonals are finite: resolution degree is at least -1 and complex degree at least b.

Filter the augmented total by complex degree. Its graded complexes are shifts of the augmented columns, so their homology and the first spectral-sequence page vanish. In any fixed cochain degree choose a page beyond the finitely many filtration bounds in degrees n-1, n and n+1. The cycle and boundary subquotients then stabilize to the graded pieces of total cohomology. Each is zero. Induction on the finite exhaustive separated cohomology filtration gives zero total cohomology. This is the finite-diagonal argument of Stacks 0133 applied to the augmented rows, which pins the result to aug rather than an abstract cohomology identification.
Thus the mapping cone of aug is acyclic. Apply CochainComplex.mappingCone.quasiIso_iff_acyclic to conclude that aug is a quasi-isomorphism.

theorem cartanEilenberg_augmentation_quasiIso
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vA} A]
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (I : HomologicalComplex₂ A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
    (a : ((CochainComplex.single₀ A).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      K ⟶ I)
    (hbelow : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ s : ℤ, s < b → IsZero (I.X s))
    (hrows : ∀ s : ℤ, QuasiIso (a.f s))
    (aug : K ⟶ (((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor (𝟭 A)).obj I).flip).total
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (haug : ∀ n : ℤ, aug.f n = (a.f n).f 0 ≫
      (HomologicalComplex.extendXIso
        (((𝟭 A).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (I.X n))
        ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat (i := 0) (i' := 0) rfl).inv ≫
      (((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor (𝟭 A)).obj I).flip).ιTotal
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 n n (zero_add n)) :
    QuasiIso aug
